gaps: The 2025 MINEC assessment was read only on a user-uploaded Scribd mirror. Official-host authenticity, exact model assumptions and reuse terms remain unresolved; its retained model claims are low-confidence draft context requiring human source review.
The model's territorial extent is not endorsed as a sovereignty determination. Disputed-territory tags were removed; geographic administrative claims require official verification.
No verified climate-caused armed violence or complete reverse-FCV pathway is retained. Mining violence and border/electoral insecurity are separate context.
UNICEF describes combined flooding/electoral access constraints, not identified causal effects or verified interruption of an adaptation intervention.

Flood-related evacuations and temporary movement have uncertain denominators and duration; Warao concerns and Amazonas evacuation counts must not be conflated. An undated general projection was excluded.

executive_assessment.text: Model-based regional and Indigenous vulnerability findings are low-confidence because the government report was accessible only through an unverified user-uploaded mirror.
IACHR and UNICEF provide named flood, evacuation and child-service findings. Exact caseloads, duration and group identities remain bounded by each source.
Community water and radio-referral activities add response capacities, while electoral and border-conflict constraints are separate dated context. No climate-to-armed-violence chain is inferred.
